theme: Returning an item at a store
summary_zh: 學會到店裡退換貨時的實用說法，並用 Could you tell me…／Do you know if… 這類間接問句，禮貌地問店員問題。

vocab.definition: a receipt or record that shows you bought something
vocab.example: You'll need some proof of purchase, such as a receipt or a bank statement.
vocab.example_zh: 你需要提供購買證明，例如收據或銀行對帳單。

vocab.definition: money you can only spend in the same shop instead of getting cash back
vocab.example: Without a receipt, they could only give me store credit.
vocab.example_zh: 因為沒有收據，他們只能給我店內購物金。

vocab.definition: not working properly because something is wrong with it
vocab.example: If the item is faulty, you can return it even after thirty days.
vocab.example_zh: 如果商品有瑕疵，即使超過三十天也可以退。

vocab.definition: a fee some stores charge when you return something that isn't broken
vocab.example: Opened electronics come with a 10% restocking fee.
vocab.example_zh: 已拆封的電子產品要收 10% 的重新上架費。

vocab.definition: the box and wrapping that a product came in when you bought it
vocab.example: Please bring the lamp back in its original packaging.
vocab.example_zh: 請把檯燈連同原包裝一起帶回來。

vocab.definition: the number of days after buying something when the shop will still take it back
vocab.example: The return window for sale items is only fourteen days.
vocab.example_zh: 特價商品的可退貨期限只有十四天。

vocab.definition: without asking you to explain why
vocab.example: They'll take back any shoes within a month, no questions asked.
vocab.example_zh: 一個月內的鞋子他們都收退，不問理由。

vocab.definition: to give one thing back and get a different one in its place
vocab.example: Could I swap this one for a smaller size?
vocab.example_zh: 我可以把這件換成小一號的嗎？

reading.title: How to Take Something Back Without the Stress
paragraphs: Most of us have done it: bought something in a hurry and regretted it a week later. Maybe your allergies flared up and you grabbed the first air purifier you saw, or you panic-bought a heater before the cold weather arrived. Returning it should be simple, but many people feel awkward at the counter.

Start by checking the return window. Most stores print it at the bottom of the receipt, so you can see it at a glance. Some shops will take anything back within thirty days, no questions asked, whereas others give you only two weeks for sale items. Keep the original packaging if you can, and bring proof of purchase. A photo of the receipt on your phone is usually fine.

Next, know what you can't return. Opened over-the-counter medicine almost never goes back on the shelf, and some electronics come with a restocking fee unless they are faulty. If you don't have a receipt, many stores will still offer store credit. Ask whether any unused balance carries over or expires at the end of the year.

Finally, be polite but clear. Questions like "Could you tell me what my options are?" work better than "Why can't I get a refund?" Staff hear complaints all day, and most will try harder for a calm customer. And if the shop has just announced a price hike, it may be worth asking if you can swap the item for a newer model at the old price. If you're a member, ask whether your membership comes with any extra return days, especially if your renewal is coming up.

questions.q: According to the article, what is usually acceptable as proof of purchase?
options: A photo of the receipt on your phone
The original packaging
Your membership card
The price tag on the item
questions.explain_zh: 第二段最後：A photo of the receipt on your phone is usually fine. 原包裝是另外建議保留的東西，不是購買證明。

questions.q: Which item is the hardest to return, according to the third paragraph?
options: A faulty electronic device
Opened over-the-counter medicine
A heater bought on sale
Anything bought without a receipt
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：Opened over-the-counter medicine almost never goes back on the shelf. 有瑕疵的電子產品反而不收重新上架費；沒收據通常還能拿購物金。

questions.q: What can we infer about asking "Could you tell me what my options are?"
options: It means the customer has no receipt.
It is too formal for most shops.
It sounds calm, so staff are more likely to help.
It is the only way to get store credit.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：最後一段說這種問法比 Why can't I get a refund? 好，因為 most will try harder for a calm customer，可推論這樣問聽起來冷靜有禮，店員比較願意幫忙。

grammar.point: Indirect questions: Could you tell me where…
grammar.point_zh: 間接問句：Could you tell me where…（禮貌地問問題）

guide.key_zh: Could you tell me／Do you know 後面改用「主詞＋動詞」順序，不加 do／does／did。

uses.label_zh: 問 wh- 問題（哪裡、什麼時候、多久…）
uses.form: Could you tell me + where / when / how long + S + V
uses.signal: Could you tell me / Do you know
uses.note_zh: where is it → where it is

uses.label_zh: 問「是不是／有沒有」（yes/no 問題）
uses.form: Do you know + if / whether + S + V
uses.note_zh: 原本沒有疑問詞，就補 if 或 whether

uses.label_zh: 用直述句帶出問題，更委婉
uses.form: I was wondering + if / wh- + S + V
uses.signal: I was wondering / I'd like to know

mistakes.wrong: Could you tell me where is the returns desk?
mistakes.right: Could you tell me where the returns desk is?
mistakes.why_zh: 間接問句裡要用直述句順序：主詞 the returns desk 放在 is 前面

mistakes.wrong: Do you know when does the store close?
mistakes.right: Do you know when the store closes?
mistakes.why_zh: 不加 does，動詞直接變化：the store closes

mistakes.wrong: Can you tell me do you have this in black?
mistakes.right: Can you tell me if you have this in black?
mistakes.why_zh: yes/no 問題要用 if 或 whether 接起來

examples.en: Could you tell me where the returns desk is?
examples.zh: 可以請你告訴我退貨櫃台在哪裡嗎？

examples.en: Do you know if I can get a refund without a receipt?
examples.zh: 你知道沒有收據能不能退款嗎？

examples.en: I was wondering whether I could swap this for a newer model.
examples.zh: 我在想，不知道能不能把這台換成新一點的型號。

exercises.q: Excuse me, could you tell me where the fitting rooms ___ (be)?
exercises.explain_zh: 間接問句用直述句順序：the fitting rooms are。主詞是複數，所以用 are，放在句尾。

exercises.q: Could you tell me when you ___ (buy) it? Was it last Monday?
exercises.explain_zh: 有明確的過去時間點（last Monday），用過去式 bought。間接問句不加 did，所以不是 when did you buy。

exercises.q: Do you know how long you ___ (have) the purifier? Since August?
exercises.explain_zh: Since August 是從過去持續到現在，用現在完成式 have had。have 是狀態動詞，不說 have been having。

exercises.q: Do you know whether the store ___ (change) its return policy since last year?
exercises.explain_zh: since last year 到現在，用現在完成式；主詞 the store 是單數，所以用 has changed，不是 have changed。

options: what time does the store close
what time the store closes
what time closes the store
what time is the store closes
exercises.explain_zh: 間接問句不加 does，用直述句順序「主詞＋動詞」：what time the store closes。

exercises.q: I was wondering ___ I could get store credit instead.
options: if
that
what
do
exercises.explain_zh: 原本是 yes/no 問題（Can I get store credit?），要用 if 或 whether 接起來。that 用在陳述事實，不能用來問問題。

listening.title: At the Returns Desk

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ethan
lines.text: Hi, I'd like to return this air purifier. Could you tell me if I'm in the right line?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: You are. Can I ask why you're bringing it back?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ethan
lines.text: My allergies flared up last month, so I bought it in a hurry. But it's been making a loud clicking noise for about a week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Sorry to hear that. Do you know when you bought it? I'll need some proof of purchase.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ethan
lines.text: On October twentieth. I've got the receipt on my phone, and I kept the original packaging.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Perfect. Since it's faulty, there's no restocking fee, and you're still within the thirty-day return window.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ethan
lines.text: Great. Actually, I was wondering whether I could swap it for the newer model instead.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: You can, but after the price hike it's forty dollars more. Or I can give you a full refund.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ethan
lines.text: Hmm. Could you tell me how long the refund takes to reach my card?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Grace
lines.text: Usually three to five business days. Store credit is instant, though, and any balance you don't use just carries over to your next visit.

questions.q: Why is Ethan returning the air purifier?
options: It was too expensive.
It has been making a loud noise.
His allergies have gone away.
He bought the wrong size.
questions.explain_zh: Ethan 說：it's been making a loud clicking noise for about a week. 機器一直發出喀喀聲。過敏是他當初買的原因，不是退貨原因。

questions.q: Why doesn't Ethan have to pay a restocking fee?
options: Because he is a member
Because he kept the original packaging
Because the purifier is faulty
Because he wants store credit
questions.explain_zh: Grace 說：Since it's faulty, there's no restocking fee. 因為商品有瑕疵，所以不收重新上架費。

questions.q: What can we infer from Grace's last answer?
options: Ethan cannot get a refund at all.
The newer model is cheaper than the old one.
Store credit is faster to use than a refund.
Ethan's membership ends this week.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：退款要 three to five business days 才會到卡上，而 Store credit is instant，可推論購物金比退款更快就能用。

dictation: I've got the receipt on my phone, and I kept the original packaging.

writing.task: You bought a pair of headphones online, and one side has stopped working. Write a short email to the shop in three short paragraphs: (1) the problem, (2) what you've done so far, and (3) what you'd like next. Ask at least two indirect questions. Don't join two complete sentences with only a comma.
writing.task_zh: 你在網路上買了一副耳機，現在有一邊沒聲音了。寫一封短信給店家，分三小段：(1) 問題是什麼；(2) 你目前做了什麼；(3) 你希望接下來怎麼處理。至少用兩個間接問句。不要只用逗號把兩個完整的句子接在一起。
writing.sample:
Hello,

I bought a pair of wireless headphones from your website on November 2. Last week, the left side stopped working. I think the headphones are faulty.

So far, I've charged them fully and reset them twice. I've also tried them with two different phones. Nothing has worked, and the left side is still silent.

Could you tell me how I can send them back? I'd also like to know whether I can swap them for a new pair instead of getting a refund. I still have the original packaging and the order confirmation.

Thank you,
Ethan
checklist_zh: 有沒有分成三小段：問題、目前做了什麼、接下來希望怎麼處理
間接問句用直述句順序：Could you tell me how I can…（不是 how can I）
yes/no 問題用 whether 或 if 接起來
so far 後面用現在完成式（I've charged、I've tried）
沒有只用逗號把兩個完整的句子接在一起

reading.title: The Hidden Cost of Free Returns
paragraphs: A decade ago, sending something back to a shop was a hassle. You needed the receipt, the box, and a good excuse. Then online retailers discovered that generous return policies sell more stuff. If customers know they can send things back for free, no questions asked, they stop agonizing over every purchase and simply click "buy." Free returns became a selling point, and brick-and-mortar stores had little choice but to follow suit.

The trouble is that returns aren't free for anyone in the long run. Someone has to inspect each item, repack it and decide whether it can be resold. A surprising amount of what comes back can't be sold again. Clothes that have been tried on at home come back creased or stained, and electronics without their original packaging often end up being sold off cheaply in bulk. Some of it ends up in landfills, which hardly fits the green image many brands like to project.

As a result, retailers are now quietly tightening the rules. Return windows are getting shorter, restocking fees are creeping back, and a few big names have started charging to return items that aren't faulty. Others are taking a softer approach, flagging customers who return an unusually high share of what they buy, or offering store credit instead of a refund.

None of this means shoppers are the villains. After all, sizes vary wildly from brand to brand, and photos online can be misleading. But the era of treating your living room as a free fitting room may be drawing to a close. The smart move is to ask before you buy: "Could you tell me what your return policy is, and whether it covers this item?"

questions.q: Why did online shops start offering free returns?
options: Because the law required them to
Because it made people buy more
Because returned items were easy to resell
Because brick-and-mortar stores did it first
questions.explain_zh: 第一段：generous return policies sell more stuff，顧客知道可以免費退，就不會猶豫直接下單。實體店是後來才跟進（follow suit）。

questions.q: What does the writer suggest about brands that send returned goods to landfills?
options: They are breaking the law.
Their actions don't match the eco-friendly image they promote.
They have no other way to deal with faulty goods.
They are mostly small, local shops.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第二段說這種做法 hardly fits the green image many brands like to project，暗示這些品牌宣傳環保形象，實際作法卻不相符。

questions.q: What is the writer's overall attitude toward shoppers?
options: Shoppers are mainly to blame for the problem.
Shoppers should never return clothes.
Shoppers aren't the bad guys, but they should check policies before buying.
Shoppers should only buy from physical stores.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：最後一段先說 None of this means shoppers are the villains，再建議 ask before you buy。作者不怪消費者，但建議買之前先問清楚退貨規定。

listening.title: Not Quite the Right Shade

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Nina
lines.text: Hi, um, I'd like to return this sofa cover. It was delivered on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: Sure. Is there anything wrong with it, or—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Nina
lines.text: No, no, it's not faulty. It's just… the color looked completely different online. It's more orange than rust.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: Ah, yeah, we get that a lot with that one, honestly. Do you have the order number handy?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Nina
lines.text: Right here. Could you tell me whether there's a fee? A friend said you'd started charging for returns.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: Only for online returns sent back by mail. Since you've brought it in yourself, it's free.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Nina
lines.text: Oh, thank goodness. And do you know if you have it in a darker shade?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: Let me check… There's a deep brown in our warehouse, but it's ten dollars more, and it won't be out on the floor until Friday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Nina
lines.text: Hmm. I'd rather see it in person this time. Could I just swap it for store credit and come back on the weekend?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Leo
lines.text: Absolutely. I'll load it onto a store card now, and it doesn't expire, so there's no rush.

questions.q: Why is Nina returning the sofa cover?
options: It arrived damaged.
It was delivered late.
The color isn't what she expected.
It's the wrong size.
questions.explain_zh: Nina 說 it's not faulty，問題是 the color looked completely different online，顏色和網路上看到的不一樣。

questions.q: Why doesn't Nina have to pay a fee?
options: She returned it in person.
The item is faulty.
She is buying a more expensive cover.
She has the order number.
questions.explain_zh: Leo 說只有郵寄的網路退貨才收費：Since you've brought it in yourself, it's free.

questions.q: What can we infer about Nina from her last request?
options: She has decided not to buy anything else from the shop.
She doesn't want to repeat the mistake she made buying online.
She thinks the deep brown cover is too expensive to consider.
She needs the money back immediately.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：她說 I'd rather see it in person this time，表示這次想親眼看過顏色再買，不想再犯網購看錯顏色的錯。

dictation: Could you tell me whether there's a fee? A friend said you'd started charging for returns.
Since you've brought it in yourself, it's free.
